Builds 3D models. (builds primitive shapes in code and puts them into one vertex array)

Builds vertex arrays for drawing toon 3D (clay-like single-color material and outline). Comes from the board 3D of webgame-rimminer. (same form as three.js primitive geometries)
  - Shapes are built in their own coordinates with the center at the origin. When adding a part, position, rotation and scale are multiplied in and it is put into one chunk.
  - One vertex is position 3, normal 3, color 3 (sRGB), material 2 (glow strength, unlit), pattern 4 (pattern number, pattern color). The meaning of pattern number and color is decided by the drawing shader. (0 means no pattern)
  - Texture coordinates (UV) are stored separately, 2 per vertex, in uvData outside the vertex array. If even one vertex has UV given, the rest are filled with 0. (the shape's uvs, addTriangles' uvs)
    (0, 0) is the top left of the image. (same as glTF) Boxes are 0 ~ 1 per face, spheres are 0 ~ 1 by longitude and latitude.
  - A material range (materialRanges) is the span of body vertex indices that holds one material. The GLB reader stores one per primitive. (material name, extras, texture, indexStart, indexCount of ToonRenderer.drawMesh)
  - The outline is a slightly enlarged copy of the part. It is stored separately since only back faces are drawn. (inverted hull)
  - Triangle winding is adjusted by looking at vertex normals so the outside becomes the front face. (back-face culling and outline rely on winding)

3D camera. (holds a perspective or orthographic projection and the viewpoint, recomputes the view and projection matrices only when they change)
- Coordinates are right-handed with y up, same as the engine's Matrix4. The camera looks down -Z. (createLookAt, createPerspective)
- Perspective: setPerspective(field of view, near distance, far distance), orthographic: setOrthographic(visible height, near distance, far distance).
  The aspect ratio is given separately with setAspectRatio. (update it whenever the drawing rectangle changes, orthographic width is height x ratio)
- lookAt(eye, target, up) sets the viewpoint.
- getViewProjectionMatrix returns the cached matrix. It recomputes only on the first read after a function that changes values is called.
  Do not modify the returned matrix. (clone to modify)
- The renderer (ToonRenderer.beginFrameWithCamera) and the 2D display (projectToView) share the same camera, to put text or buttons over 3D points.
- projectToView(x, y, z, viewRect): a world point to a position in viewRect. viewRect is the rectangle the 3D is drawn in, given in the caller's coordinates (usually view coordinates).
- unprojectToPlane(viewPosition, planeHeight, viewRect): the point where the line of sight from a position in viewRect meets the horizontal plane at height planeHeight (y = planeHeight).
- Raw matrices: setMatrices(view, projection) uses the matrices the game computed as is. (oblique orthographic, a projection multiplied by a screen transform, and so on) All the functions above run on those matrices.
  The view matrix is given as a rigid world → camera transform (the camera looks down -Z). Eye, target (1 in front of the eye), up and isOrthographic are extracted from that matrix.
  Field of view, visible height, near distance, far distance and aspect ratio stay as last given. Calling setPerspective, setOrthographic or lookAt discards the raw matrices and returns to the computed path.

- The lists are fonts.json (index [{ group, manifest }]) and fonts-<group>.json (subsets [{ file, weight, unicodeRange }]).

Draws all on-screen languages under one font name (the family of configureUiFont).
Latin and Cyrillic use the base font (Exo 2), and other scripts use fonts with a similar feel.
Font files are not merged. A FontFace is created for each subset split by Google Fonts and registered with that subset's character range (unicode-range).
So the browser downloads only the subsets containing characters used on screen. (Korean, Chinese and Japanese fonts have hundreds of subsets)
Characters shared by several fonts, such as Han characters, are drawn by the font registered later. The selected language's font group is registered right before Latin (second from the end)
so that Japanese gets Japanese-font Han characters and Traditional Chinese gets Traditional-font ones. Latin is always last, so digits and Latin letters use the Latin font in every language.
Subsets under one font name must all declare the same weight to be selected together by character range. (because the weight is chosen first and only subsets of that weight are considered)
So every subset is registered with only the two weights in configureUiFont's weights (initially 500, 700). Variable-weight subsets are registered twice (500 and 700), and 400-only subsets as 500.
When the screen requests 400, the 500 subset draws, and for 600 the 700 subset draws.
The canvas does not wait for subsets not yet downloaded and draws with another font, so subsets for the characters to be drawn are fetched in advance. (loadUiFontText)
When a subset is downloaded, the engine (EngineConfiguration.rebakeTextOnFontLoad) discards and rebakes only the text images baked with that subset's characters.
The font lists are split per group. (fonts.json is the index, fonts-<group>.json holds that group's subsets)
At first only the lists for the selected language and Latin are fetched, and the rest (language names in the language window, other scripts such as person names) are fetched a little after play starts.
Initial subsets are waited for only up to configureUiFont's waitMilliseconds, after which play starts first and text is rebaked as subsets arrive. (shorter first load)
Paths are written as literal strings so the build's cache busting can add fingerprints. (subset fingerprints are added to the lists by the build)
UI 노드.\n- 기존 WorldNode 계열과 다른 별도 노선의 UI:
UI node.
- A UI node on a separate track from the existing WorldNode family.
- The area is defined by 8 solver variables (left / right / top / bottom / width / height
  + derived centerX / centerY), and the user places constraints on the LayoutSolver
  to determine those values.
- This class holds the variables and the essential constraints (right == left + width, bottom == top
  + height, centerX == left + width/2, centerY == top + height/2), and registers these 4
  automatically.
- User constraints are registered with addConstraint(constraint).
- The solver is attached with setSolver(solver). When operating the whole tree together, set it only on the root UINode
  and the caller manages it so that children receive the same instance through setSolver.
- intrinsicContentSize / contentHuggingPriority / contentCompressionResistancePriority
  follow the same idea as UIKit's APIs of the same name. Subclasses override getIntrinsicContentSize.
- layoutMargins / layoutMarginsGuide follow the same idea as UIKit's UIView.layoutMargins /
  layoutMarginsGuide. The guide, in the form of a child UINode, is exposed lazily.

UI scale.
- The fixed side of the view (height for portrait, width for landscape) always has the same length, so on a small screen (a portal's PC iframe, etc.)
  one view unit becomes much smaller than 1 CSS pixel on screen and text becomes unreadable. In that case it computes a scale that enlarges only the UI layer on screen. (the game's graphics stay as they are)
- If one unit is smaller than minimumCssScale CSS pixels, it enlarges by that much. (1 ~ maximumScale)
  - On a short screen, it does not enlarge so far that the enlarged UI layer's height falls below minimumLayerHeight. (so the top and bottom UI do not cover the screen in phone landscape, 0 means not checked)
  - On a portrait screen (width at most portraitRatio times the height), it enlarges without an upper limit so that one unit becomes minimumCssScale CSS pixels.
- Usage: const uiScale = UIScale.read(viewWidth, viewHeight); layerNode.setLocalScale(Vector2.create(uiScale, uiScale));
  UIWindowLayer enlarges windows by this scale.

UI scene.
- Standalone base scene that directly inherits Scene.
- Has its own common infrastructure identical to GameScene (developer tools / touch routing / loading screen /
  env() safe-area insets / automatic viewSize detection / canvas background clear).
- Has its own LayoutSolver instance. Calls updateVariables automatically every tick.
- Has its own screen guide UINode (screenNode). Fixed at top-left (0, 0), with width/height
  registered as edit variables and updated via suggestValue on resize.
  (same idea as UIKit's UIWindow.bounds)
- Has a separate safeAreaLayoutGuide UINode. Represents the area inset from screenNode by
  safeAreaInsets. (same idea as UIKit's UIView.safeAreaLayoutGuide)
  In the layout() phase, env() insets are automatically applied to setSafeAreaInsets.
- UINodes added to the tree are automatically attached to the solver on tick.

고정 걸음.\n- 프레임 간격이 들쭉날쭉해도 규칙(물리, 판의 흐름)은:
Fixed step.
- Even if frame intervals are uneven, rules (physics, round flow) always run at the same step (stepSeconds).
- advance(timeDelta, stepFunction) accumulates the received time and calls stepFunction(stepSeconds) each time a full step accumulates.
  The returned value is the remaining fraction (0 ~ 1). Drawing by blending the previous step and the current step by this fraction keeps the steps from jittering against the screen refresh rate.
- Runs at most maximumStepsPerFrame steps per frame. If time still remains after that many, the remaining time is discarded.
  (So a slow device does not get even slower by running the backlog all at once after a stall)
- If stepFunction returns false, this frame's steps stop there and the remaining time stays accumulated. (For holding briefly, as in meetings or cutscenes)

Image with a shadow.
- Draws the image (or one piece of an atlas) inside the node as large as possible while keeping its ratio, centered.
- Like ShadowText, bakes the look of the shadow painted beneath the image's shape (opacity) into one canvas and draws that single sheet.
  The node's opacity applies to the image and shadow as one sheet.
- If an image color is given, paints the image as a single-color shape of that color. (e.g. a wrap that places the original image on top at the same spot so only the shadow remains)
- Rebakes when the draw scale (device DPR, view scale), image, color, shadow or node size changes. Widens the edge by the shadow blur amount.
그림자를 깐 한 줄 글.\n- 글자 노드 두 벌(같은 글을 검게 밑에,:
Single-line text with a shadow.
- Laying a shadow with two text nodes (the same text in black below, the text on top) makes the two show through separately, so when the node is faded the shadow beneath shows through the faded text.
  This component bakes the look of the text placed over the shadow into one canvas and draws that single sheet, so the node's opacity applies to the text and shadow as one sheet.
- Horizontal alignment and placement use the same calculation as Graphic.drawTextEntry. Vertically it is the node's center.
- If the text exceeds the node width, it shrinks from the initial size down to the minimum ratio (setFitMinimumRatio) to fit.
- Rebakes when the draw scale (device DPR, view scale), text, style or node width changes, or when a new web font chunk is downloaded.
- The shadow can be painted with the canvas shadow so that it blurs. The baked canvas edge is widened by the blur amount.
- Italic, underline, strikethrough (setItalic, setUnderline, setStrikethrough): the line position and thickness are the same as Text's middle baseline, and the lines are baked together with the text so the shadow lies beneath them too.
- Text direction is "ltr", "rtl", "auto" (by the first strong character of the text).

Node layout.
- A fluent builder that declaratively composes the node hierarchy without local variables.
- A structure similar to Unreal Slate / Flutter widgets.
- Specifies all positions/sizes with number pairs (x, y) without Vector2.
- Specifies the node type with create(nodeClass). (default: WorldNode)

Example:
  const panel = NodeLayout.create(WorldNode)
      .pivot(Pivot.middleCenter)
      .contentSize(680, 900)
      .component(Paint, (c) => { c.setColor(new Color(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 1)); })
      .children(
          NodeLayout.create(WorldNode)
              .contentSize(120, 70)
              .component(Text, (c) => { c.setText("OK"); })
      )
      .build();

Expands the press area.
- Keeps the visible button as is, and places a transparent press area as the sibling right behind the button to widen its width and height to at least the minimum size. (easier to press with a finger)
- The node later in draw order receives the press, so presses on the button are received by the button and only the widened part around the button is received by the press area.
- Pressing the press area calls the button's click notification as is. If the button is turned off or cannot be pressed, the press area follows.
- Follows the button's position, size and pivot every frame, so it stays matched even when the screen re-places the button.
- If a clipping node is set, clips the widened part so it does not go outside that node's screen rectangle. (the button's own area stays as is, so that areas outside the window or the scroll box are not pressed)
  Clipping is correct when the parent does not rotate.

Multi-level bloom effect. (extracts the bright part at half size, blurs it while halving the size, then adds it back to the level above while doubling the size)
- Each level is half the size of the previous level. The first level (half the scene size) is the result. (getResultTexture)
- Extraction: from the average of four source samples, the part whose brightness (the largest of the three channels) exceeds the threshold. Within the knee width around the threshold it comes in smoothly. (setThreshold(threshold, knee))
- Downsampling is a dual filter mixing the center four and the four corners (one diagonal step), and upsampling is a nine-tap tent.
- With useFloatColor the targets are RGBA16F, so bright values above 1 are blurred as they are. (for HDR scenes, with RGBA8 they are clipped at 1)
- Usage: resize(scene width, height) → render(scene texture) → getResultTexture() is multiplied by the strength and added in the composite pass.
- Side effects: disables the depth test and blending, makes TEXTURE0 active, and changes the framebuffer binding. The blend function is restored to the previous one.

- Bakes the chosen characters in one font and one size into a glyph atlas (a single canvas), and when drawing text it cuts the glyphs out of the atlas.
  Every character uses the same image, so sprite batching is not broken. (unlike Text, which bakes a texture per string)
  Used where characters change often and the same characters are drawn many times, such as scores, damage numbers and clocks.

셰이더 미리 링크.\n- ShaderProgram 은 링크하자마자 결과를:
Shader pre-linking.
- ShaderProgram queries the result right after linking, so the main thread stalls until linking finishes. Building several shaders at once on first draw makes that frame stutter.
- At startup (during the logo, loading), linking the same sources in the background with KHR_parallel_shader_compile leaves them in the browser's program cache, so later when ShaderProgram builds the same sources it finishes quickly.
- Does nothing if the extension is absent. (Starting links without the extension can make later draw commands wait for the link and stall instead)
- Does not query link results, and deletes the programs and shaders once linked. (The cache remains, even if a source is wrong no error is raised here, the ShaderProgram at draw time reports it)
- Does not touch draw state (bound program, buffers, textures).
- Usage: new ShaderWarmer(webGL2RenderingContext, [{ vertexShader, fragmentShader, attributeLocationTable }]) then update() every frame.
  Attribute locations must be given the same as those passed to ShaderProgram to hit the cache.

Sound. (background music and sound effects)

Uses the engine's AudioManager (shared AudioContext) and AudioAsset (MP3). Plays downloaded sound buffers with Web Audio. (does not synthesize sound, only plays files)
Takes a sound table. Each row is { id, path or paths, volume, minimumInterval, isMusic, maximumVoices, pitchVariation, playSeconds, fadeOutSeconds }.
  volume: per-sound volume. (0 ~ 1)  minimumInterval: interval before the same sound can play again. (seconds, so they do not pile up and get noisy)
  paths: a group of multiple recordings of the same sound. Picks one each time it plays, never the same as the one just before. (path if only one)
  maximumVoices: number of instances of the same sound that can play at once. (beyond that the oldest is cut off, if absent up to the total number of sound effects)
  pitchVariation: ratio by which the pitch varies on each play. (0.05 means ±5%, 0 if absent)
  playSeconds, fadeOutSeconds: plays only the first playSeconds seconds of a sound effect and fades it out over fadeOutSeconds seconds. (long files, to the end if absent or 0)

Volume: background music = music volume setting × music ratio (half volume for the pause window, etc.) × sound volume, sound effect = sound effect volume setting × sound volume × volume at call time (attenuation by distance, etc.).
Background music can be crossfaded (fadeSeconds), and the stopped position is remembered per sound so it can resume from there. (isResumed)
Mute takes precedence over the volume setting. If any one of the following applies, no sound plays regardless of the settings.
  - Platform mute. (the function given with setExternalMuteProvider, the platform SDK's mute setting, while a rewarded ad is shown, etc.)
  - The user's mute button. (setUserMuted)
  - Page hidden. (another tab, app switch)
  - The window loses focus on a touch-primary device. (blur, when the app starts going to the background)
    On iPhone the page-hidden notification arrives after the app has gone to the background, by which time audio freezes without stopping and the last sound chunk repeats.
    The window focus-loss notification arrives before that. On desktop, clicking outside the canvas (the outer page) also loses focus, so it is not followed there.
Platform mute is read every frame (update), and page hiding is applied at that moment. (frames stop when hidden)
While muted, the AudioContext is also stopped. (suspend, resume when unmuted) On iPhone, if an app switch or interstitial ad takes over a running AudioContext,
no sound plays even when it is woken on return. If it is stopped on its own beforehand, sound plays again on return.
If the AudioContext is still not running after unmuting, it tries to wake it at short intervals until it runs. (iPhone sometimes ignores the wake at the moment of returning to the app)

If allowed (setAutoplayAllowedProvider, allowed if not given), it tries to wake once even before a press. If blocked, it turns on at the first press as below.
Browsers do not allow sound before the person first presses. Since the engine creates and wakes the AudioContext on the first press,
the sound paths (music and sound effect buses, AudioBus) are created after that, and sound plays only while the AudioContext is running. (so sounds requested while stopped do not all play at once on wake)
Buses are retrieved with getMusicBus and getEffectBus. Players made from a bus (AudioBus.createAudioPlayer) also follow the volume setting and mute.
The volume setting is applied directly to the bus's GainNode. So values set with the bus's setVolume and mute last only until SoundSystem applies the volume again.
Sound files are downloaded in the background so they do not block play. Sounds not yet downloaded or that failed to download simply do not play.

Sets sprite batching.
- When on, consecutive draws (images, shapes, text) using the same texture are accumulated with transform and color stored in the vertices, then drawn in a single draw call.
- When the texture, blend, clipping or swapped-in shader changes, or the buffer fills, everything accumulated so far is drawn, and the engine draws the rest at frame end.
- Gathering many images into one sheet (atlas) greatly reduces draw calls.
- When inserting a pass that handles WebGL directly (external renderer, etc.) with this on, call flushSpriteBatch() before it.

- Sprites that use the same page image are batched by the engine and drawn at once. (Graphic.setSpriteBatchingEnabled)
- Two JSON formats are read:
  1. Made by tools/atlas.cjs. { images: { "name.png": { x, y, width, height, page } }, meta: { imageFileName, pages: [{ imageFileName }] } }
     If page is absent it is page 0, and if meta.pages is absent it is the single image meta.imageFileName.
  2. Page paths and a [page, x, y, width, height] table. { pagePaths: ["path"], frames: { "name": [page, x, y, width, height] } }
- Images are found by the name with the extension removed. ("icon-close.png" is found as either "icon-close" or "icon-close.png")
- If a page path has no slash (/), it is read relative to the folder containing the JSON, and if it has one, it is read as written.
- If several atlases are added with addSearchAtlas, findFrame and applyFrame (static) search them in the order added. (earlier ones win)

Heat haze effect component.
- Takes the canvas content drawn before the attached node, over the node's area, and applies a shimmering effect.
- Therefore the effect is visible only when attached to the node drawn last (topmost) in the scene. Child nodes are drawn over the effect.
- A component attached to a node, like ParticleSystem and TrailRenderer. The area uses the node's content size (contentSize) and pivot.
  If the node's content size is empty when attached, it is set to 300 x 300.
- Usage:
    const heatHazeEffect = node.addComponent(HeatHazeEffect);
    heatHazeEffect.setAmplitude(4);
- In the WebGL Graphic, it flushes the batch first, copies the screen bounding box of the node area (drawing buffer pixels) into a texture with copyTexSubImage2D,
  and redraws it shifted along a sine curve, one quad per line, as vertex color quads (drawColoredQuads). (same method as the Rust vanilla-engine)
- If the area goes off screen, the screen edge pixels are stretched. (CLAMP_TO_EDGE)
- The copied texture is a GL resource, so call destroy() when done with it.

  - The material's baseColorFactor is a linear color so it is converted to sRGB and stored, and emissiveFactor, if present, is stored as glow. (if emissiveTexture exists, glow is passed only through the material range)
  - TEXCOORD_0, if present, is stored as uvData. A material range (materialRanges) is stored per primitive.
    { name material name, materialIndex, nodeName, indexStart, indexCount, extras material extras, alphaMode, alphaCutoff, baseColorFactor linear, emissiveFactor linear, baseColorImage, emissiveImage (index into images, -1 if none), hasUv }
    When painting separate sections within a part (accent color sections, display panels), pick by material name or extras and draw only that section with indexStart, indexCount of ToonRenderer.drawMesh.
  - Images are read with readGlbImages, decoded with decodeGlbImage and passed to ToonRenderer.createTexture.
  - In material extras, outline marks an outline shell (only back faces drawn), basic marks an unlit part.
    If outlineOptions is given, those shells are not stored, and a shell of uniform width per point is newly built from the body of nodes that have a ".outline" pair. (MeshBuilder.addTriangleShell)
  - If there is a skeleton (skin), reads the bone nodes and their inverse bind matrices, the animations and their extras (hitAt for strikes, loop "once" for play-once, etc.) together. The pose is computed by writeSkinPose.
  - Models whose parts are hidden or painted separately (like a cluster of several crystals) are read per node with readGlbNodeArrays.
    Node extras (pivot where doors and legs rotate, etc.) are stored together as that part's extras.
  - For a skinned model read as one chunk (like a vehicle), node extras, part positions and followed bones are read separately with readGlbNodeInfos.
The engine's GLB reader is tied up inside the engine's PBR model (SkinnedModel), so only the vertex arrays for toon drawing are extracted here.

- Dims the whole area (presses do not pass through to what is behind) and shows a panel in the center. The dim also covers the safe area (setViewBleed).
- The panel widens to fit the area's width but does not exceed maximumWidth. Its height is the value returned by layoutContent, and if it is larger than the area the whole panel is scaled down.
- The open and close motion is PopupMotion. When the close motion finishes, the window layer detaches it. (it does not receive presses in the meantime)
- Pressing outside (the dim) closes it. Turned off per window with setOutsideCloseEnabled. The window layer's closeTopWindow (back) also follows this value.
- Node structure: window (area size) ├ dim (dimNode, Paint + UIButton) └ frame (frameNode, panel center pivot, motion scale) └ panel (panelNode, a single Paint, content goes here)
- The panel look (decorations such as shadow, border, gloss) is up to the game. The game inherits this class, attaches decoration nodes to the frame in the constructor
  (setSiblingIndex(0) for things placed behind the panel), and overrides layoutPanel to fit them to the panel size. The default panel Paint is changed or turned off via getPanelPaint().
  For the motion shape (a panel rising from below, etc.), override applyMotion.
- The derived class places the content inside the panel in layoutContent(panelWidth) and returns the panel's height. (default is the setPanelHeight value)
- Usage:
    const window = new UIWindow("settings");
    window.getPanelNode().addChild(contentNode);
    windowLayer.openWindow(window);
    window.close();

Detects slow devices. (measures frame intervals for the first few seconds, used to automatically turn on a lightweight path that disables heavy effects)
- After measuring starts and the wait seconds pass, looks at each frame's interval during the measure seconds. (the first few seconds stutter while models and images load)
- If frames exceeding the slow multiple of the target interval (one frame at the max frame rate, or one frame at 60 if unlimited) make up at least the slow fraction, it is a slow device.
  - Why 1.4 times rather than one frame: a 90 Hz screen with max 60 has the engine draw every other refresh, so the interval is always 22 ms, and that is not the device being slow.
  - On 60 Hz and 120 Hz screens, a frame that missed one refresh (33 ms, 25 ms) counts as slow. One in four means below 48 fps.
- Once judged a slow device, it does not measure again. If the window is hidden before measuring finishes, restart() measures again from the start.
  If not slow, measureAgain() can measure once more in a heavy scene.
- Does not import the engine or the browser. The caller passes the frame interval and max frame rate.

Camera gestures. (gestures that rotate, pan and zoom a 3D board or map, mouse right and middle button drag, two fingers)
- The engine's input only passes press, drag and release of one finger (or any mouse button). Rotate, pan and zoom gestures are outside that, so the canvas DOM events are read separately. (the engine's behavior is left as is)
  - Dragging with the right mouse button held: rotates by the horizontal drag (the screen width is one full turn) and tilts by the vertical drag. Releasing without dragging is a right click.
  - Dragging with the middle mouse button held: pans.
  - Two fingers: dragging in the same direction pans, pinching in and out zooms in and out around the midpoint of the two fingers, and twisting past the twist threshold rotates. (prevents slight rotation while pinch-zooming)
- The wheel is passed by the engine. Here it only records whether Ctrl was held. (laptop touchpad pinches also arrive as Ctrl wheel)
- During a gesture, isGestureActive signals not to use the presses and releases passed by the engine for gameplay.
- The accumulated amounts (pan, rotate, tilt, zoom) are taken out every frame with take. Pan is in view units, rotate and tilt in radians, zoom is a ratio to multiply.
- Also reads whether the last input was a finger or a mouse. Mouse events the browser emulates right after a finger is lifted are ignored.
- Constructing attaches events to the engine's canvas. When done, dispose().

Base of toon 3D GPU effects. (The general-purpose part of the in-board effects that webgame-rimminer and aberrant each used separately)
- Texture: a single atlas built in code on the first draw, without image files. The left half is a 16-cell smoke flipbook, the right half is ToonVfxSlot cells and eight rows of color ramps.
  Ramp colors are decided by the game. (setRamps, each row is colors going from a white core to dark, an effect's ramp is the row number, -1 means color only without a ramp)
- Particles: GPU particles drawn with instancing. Written to the buffer once when emitted, and position, size and color are computed by the vertex shader from age. (Drag, gravity, stopping on the floor, streaks stretched along velocity, color ramps)
  When the cap (setParticleCapacity) is exceeded, the oldest emitted are overwritten first, and setCountRatio multiplies the emitted count by a fraction. (Phones and the lite path)
- Effect meshes: fireballs that boil with noise and cool into smoke (addFireball), shockwave rings that flow outward, tear and curl up, with a floor glow beneath (addShockwave),
  floor decals (addDecal, queueDecal), curling smoke plumes (addPlume), solid-of-revolution beams with flowing grain and a rippling surface (queueBeam),
  ribbons spread toward the camera (queueRibbon) and lightning made by winding them down (queueLightning), lightning that re-bends during its lifetime (addLightning), and point glints at a spot (queueGlint).
- Rim: the rim of glow particles, the glow and rim of ribbons, and the rim of fireballs and shockwaves cover the edges with the rim color (setRimColor) so they are visible on bright backgrounds too. (Default is additive light only)
- Brightness gain: setLookGain(look, gain) multiplies brightness per look of particles and glints. (Default 1, for making flame streaks, light rays and embers several times brighter in linear in the HDR version)
- Age and key: emitParticles, addFireball, addShockwave, addDecal, addPlume, addLightning, addFlash take options.age (seconds already elapsed, negative delays by that much) and
  options.key (event key, not emitted again if already emitted, forgotten by clear). Even if the scene re-emits events from state every frame they appear only once, and effects shown late start from that age.
  Shake (addShake) uses Shaker's exponential decay (9 per second), so passing strength x exp(-9 x age) for a late-shown event gives the same result.
- Foot shadow: queueBlobShadow is a round shade decal for that frame (ToonVfxDecalMode.shade).
- Screen: the flash (addFlash) covers the current viewport (inside the scissor if one is set) with its color at the end of draw and then fades.
  Camera shake (addShake) is computed with the engine Shaker, and the game adds the offset given by readShake to the camera's right and up.
- Which effect to emit for which event with what values (the recipe) is up to the game. The engine only takes parameters.
- Floor: if the game reports the floor height with setFloorHeightReader((x, z) => height), decals, shockwaves and smoke plumes are placed at that height, and isGrounded particles stop at that height. (0 if none)
- Clock: update(seconds) advances this base's clock. If the board stops, the effects stop too. Items passed with queue are drawn once in that frame and then cleared.
- Drawing: call draw(view, projection) after drawing the toon models. Depth test on, depth write off, blends with premultiplied alpha. Records the previous state and restores it.

Component that draws toon 3D inside the node rectangle. (Inserts a 3D pass between the 2D node tree)
- In draw: maps the node's content area (0, 0, content size) with the current transform to a rectangle in drawing buffer pixels (the bounding rectangle if rotated),
  draws the preceding 2D batch with Graphic.runExternalPass, forgets the cached state and clears depth, then sets the renderer's screen rectangle (setScreenRect) and calls the draw function.
  When done, releases the screen rectangle and restores the 2D state with restoreRenderState.
- The renderer is built on the first draw. On devices that cannot build the shaders, it is not rebuilt and 2D is drawn with the fallback draw function (setFallbackDrawCallback).
  To share one renderer across multiple nodes, pass it in with setRenderer.
- The aspect ratio of the camera (getCamera) is matched to the rectangle's ratio on every draw. 2D markers over 3D points are computed with the same camera's projectToView.
- Depth clearing: inside a parent Mask's clip there is the Adreno 660 pitfall (Graphic.clearDepthBuffer header). The side that applies the clip
  calls clearDepthBuffer before beginClipRect, and this component is set with setDepthCleared(false).
- Draw function: (renderer, camera, screenRect, webGL2RenderingContext) => void. screenRect is { x, y, width, height } in drawing buffer pixels.
  Usually queue into ToonDrawQueue and call queue.draw(renderer, camera), or draw between renderer.beginFrameWithCamera and endFrame.
  When using ToonPostProcess, call renderer.clearScreenRect(), draw into a float render target, then give the rectangle as the viewport of end.
툰 HDR 마무리. (실수 렌더 타겟에 그린 선형 색을 블룸, 노출, 톤: Toon HDR finishing. (outputs linear color drawn to a float render target to the screen with bloom, exposure, tone mapping and gamma)

Toon HDR finishing. (outputs linear color drawn to a float render target to the screen with bloom, exposure, tone mapping and gamma)
- Combines RenderTarget (half-float color, depth), BloomEffect (or MultiLevelBloomEffect) and FullscreenPass.
- Usage: after ToonRenderer.setHdrOutput(true), begin(background linear color) → draw with ToonRenderer → end(output framebuffer, viewport)
  end (resolves first if multisampled) computes bloom and draws the tone-mapped color into the output framebuffer (screen if null).
- Constructor options: new ToonPostProcess(gl, width, height, { sampleCount, useFloatColor, depthBits, useDepthTexture }) (without options, same as now: RGBA16F, depth 16, no multisampling)
  If sampleCount is 2 or more, the scene is drawn to a multisampled (MSAA) renderbuffer and resolved to a texture before end. Reduced to a count the device supports. (getSampleCount, setSampleCount)
  depthBits 24 means 24-bit depth. (scenes with a distant far plane) useDepthTexture keeps the scene depth as a texture. (used by setLitArea)
- Color space: linear color is written to the scene render target. (ToonRenderer.setHdrOutput(true), ToonScreenOutline.setHdrOutput(true), ToonVfx colors are also treated as linear)
  Games that wrote gamma-encoded color g to the float target and converted back with g^2.2 in compositing should convert those values to linear beforehand. Colors become c^2.2, and a brightness multiplier k applied on the gamma side becomes linear k^2.2.
  (e.g. 1.37 is linear 2, 1.6 is 2.81, 2.08 is 5, brightness 1.6 with multiplier 1.6 gives (1.6 x 1.6)^2.2 = 7.9) Bloom threshold and knee are linear brightness.
- Devices that cannot use float targets: even with useFloatColor (default true), if ToonPostProcess.isFloatColorSupported is false, RGBA8 targets are built. (getUseFloatColor is false)
  That case and useFloatColor: false take the LDR path. The scene is drawn in screen color (gamma-encoded color, ToonRenderer.setHdrOutput(false)), and compositing adds bloom without tone mapping and gamma and applies only color grading.
- Bloom: default is a half-resolution 9-tap Gaussian (BloomEffect, threshold 0.9 ~ 1.6, ping-pong targets RGBA8, RGBA16F with setBloomFloatColor).
  Giving setBloomLevels(level count, threshold, knee) a level count of 1 or more switches to MultiLevelBloomEffect (halves down then scales up with a tent filter while adding, targets at the same precision as the scene). 0 restores the default. Strength is applied to both by setBloom.
- Tone mapping is the ACES approximation (Narkowicz). Exposure (setExposure) is multiplied in before mapping, then sRGB gamma is applied.
- Color grading: after gamma, applies in order brightness (setBrightness, toward 1 inside the lit area setLitArea), saturation, color tone (multiplies a color normalized to brightness 1), fog light (pulls dark areas toward that color), contrast, edge darkening. (setColorGrade, setVignette)
  Defaults are brightness 1, saturation 1, contrast 1, color tone 0, fog light 0, edge 0, so there is no grading.
- Resolution scale: with setResolutionScale(scale), the scene target is built at output size x scale and scaled up to end's viewport (linear filtering) for output. (to render only 3D at a lower resolution while leaving UI at device pixels, default 1)
- Outputting inside a node rectangle: resize(rectangle width, height) → begin → draw (leave ToonRenderer's screen rectangle cleared) → end(null, [x, drawing buffer height - y - height, width, height]).
툰 그리기 줄. (한 프레임에 그릴 모형을 담아 두었다가 ToonRend: Toon draw queue. (holds the models to draw in a frame, then draws them in order with ToonRenderer)

Toon draw queue. (holds the models to draw in a frame, then draws them in order with ToonRenderer)
- Order: stage beforeOpaque → opaque bodies → afterOpaque → outlines of opaque things → afterOutline → transparent things (farthest from the camera first, no depth writes) → afterTransparent.
  Outlines are drawn together after all bodies to switch programs less, and transparent things are blended last, far first, so things behind show through.
- Transparent: drawn alpha or tintColor alpha less than 1, or blendMode not alpha. Their outlines (hasOutline) are drawn with them.
- Groups: transparent things with the same options.group are sorted as one lump by their center depth (average of the contents) and drawn in the order added.
  If any in the group has options.isDepthPrepassed, that lump draws depth first, then paints color only on pixels at the same depth (LEQUAL).
  A hologram of many overlapping parts shows through as one lump instead of being doubly bright. Lumps show through each other since they go far first.
- Stage callbacks: callback(renderer, webGL2RenderingContext) of addPass(stage, callback) is called at that point. After the call, the renderer re-applies the frame's draw state.
- Instanced groups (addMeshInstanced) draw bodies and outlines in one go when opaque, and when transparent are sorted as one lump by the center of the instance positions.
- Shadows: drawShadows(renderer, shadowMap) draws only opaque things whose castsShadow is not false into shadow depth. Call it before draw.
- Usage: every frame clear() → addMesh / addMeshInstanced / addPass → (drawShadows) → draw(renderer, camera) or drawWithMatrices(renderer, view matrix, projection matrix)
  draw calls renderer.beginFrameWithCamera(camera) and endFrame itself. drawWithMatrices calls beginFrameWithMatrices. (orthographic raw matrix camera)
  Set the screen rectangle (ToonRenderer.setScreenRect) before that. clear empties all queued models and stage callbacks.

Toon renderer. (draws ToonMesh and ToonGlb arrays with single-color material and outline)
- Lighting: holds one ToonLightSet as default. Sun (direction and color), ambient light from sky color and ground color, fill light, rim light, specular, point lights (up to TOON_MAXIMUM_POINT_LIGHTS), bands (band count or ramp), light model (÷π).
  setLight, setSunDirection, setFillLight, setRimLight, setSpecular, setPointLights, setPointLightLimit, setBandCount, setBandRamp, setLightModel modify the default set.
  A different set (createLightSet) can be given per draw via options.lightSet. The meaning of the sun direction (the direction light travels) is in the ToonLightSet header comment.
- Material: vertex color (sRGB), glow (multiplied by the base color and added), unlit. If vertex UVs (arrays.uvData, 2 each) exist, textures are sampled.
- Draw options (options, defaults give the same image as before):
  tintColor [r, g, b, a] sRGB and alpha. If tintAmount is given (0 ~ 1), the tint is mixed in sRGB instead of multiplied. (hit flash, malfunction red)
  glowScale multiplier for vertex glow (default 1), colorScale multiplier for the final linear color (default 1, darkens mirrored reflections), emissiveColor [r, g, b] sRGB and emissiveIntensity (linear multiplier, default 1, color default black).
  baseColorTexture (multiplied into base color, alpha into opacity), emissiveTexture (multiplied into glow color), uvTransform [u offset, v offset, u scale, v scale] (offset, scale of KHR_texture_transform).
  decalTexture overlays the base color by alpha (color = texture x decalColor). Glows in that color by decalEmission. decalUvTransform is for picking one cell of an atlas.
  alphaCutoff discards pixels whose opacity is below it. (0 disables, glTF MASK)
  blendMode: ToonBlendMode.alpha (default, straight alpha), premultiplied (premultiplied alpha), additive (additive). If not alpha, drawn as translucent.
  softEdge multiplies opacity by pow(|dot(N, V)|, softEdge) to fade the edges. (0 disables, Fresnel style)
  isMirrored draws with flipped winding. If not given, flips automatically when the model matrix determinant is negative. If the view matrix is mirrored, that is added to the flip as well.
  indexStart, indexCount draw only that span of the body vertex indices. (GLB material range, hidden parts) outlineIndexStart, outlineIndexCount are for the outline shell.
  material (ToonMaterial), textures ({ uniform name: texture }), onBeforeDraw(program, webGL2RenderingContext, ToonProgramKind) are extension points. (toonmaterial.js header comment)
  lightSet (ToonLightSet) is the light set for that draw.
- Outline: draws only the back faces of the shell built by MeshBuilder.
- Skeleton: passes the bone matrices computed by writeSkinPose to drawMesh. (up to TOON_MAXIMUM_JOINTS)
- GPU instancing: drawMeshInstanced draws many copies of the same model at once with a matrix and tint per instance. (both body and outline, culled and uploaded on every draw)
  For long-lived instances, build a persistent buffer with createInstanceLayout and createInstanceBuffer and draw with drawMeshInstanceBuffer. (no culling, the material vertex snippet reads user attributes)
- Off-screen culling: tests the model's bounding sphere against the view-projection frustum and skips drawing if outside. (instances are culled one by one and only the rest are uploaded)
- Shadows: cast into a ShadowMap with beginShadowPass and drawMesh, received with setShadow. (3x3 PCF)
  Even when not receiving shadows, a 1x1 comparison depth texture is bound to the shadow unit. (if a sampler2DShadow unit has no depth texture the Mac driver reports it, and if a color texture is bound WebGL refuses to draw)
- HDR: setHdrOutput(true) outputs linear color without gamma. Draw into a float render target (ToonPostProcess) and finish with bloom and tone mapping.
- Usage: createMesh(arrays) → every frame beginFrame(view and projection) → drawMesh / drawMeshInstanced → endFrame() → deleteMesh when done.
  beginFrame records the previous draw state (blending, depth, face culling, program, vertex array) and enables depth testing and face culling, and endFrame restores the recorded state.
  (when inserting between engine 2D draws, call Graphic.flushSpriteBatch before that)
  beginFrameWithMatrices(view, projection) starts with two matrices. (orthographic raw-matrix camera) The camera position (specular, rim, soft edge) is read from view and projection.
- Per program, frame values (view and projection, camera, shadow, HDR) and the light set are uploaded only when they change. Only per-draw values (model matrix, tint, textures) are uploaded every time.
- readProgramSources(material, instanceLayout) provides the sources to pass to ShaderWarmer.
- Drawing inside a node rectangle: given setScreenRect(x, y, width, height), beginFrame moves the view-projection clip space into that rectangle and scissors out the rest.
  The rectangle is in pixels within the viewport at beginFrame time (usually the whole drawing buffer), with the origin at the top left. (position computed with graphic.getTransformMatrix in a 2D node's draw)
  Off-screen culling uses the frustum before the move. endFrame releases the scissor. The camera's aspect ratio is matched to the rectangle's ratio. (Camera3D.setAspectRatio)
- beginFrameWithCamera(Camera3D) calls beginFrame with the camera's view and projection. Uses the same camera as 2D display (Camera3D.projectToView).
- drawMeshOutline draws only the outline shell. (when ToonDrawQueue draws all outlines together after drawing every opaque body, draws are not counted)
- Textures: createTexture(image or { width, height, data }, { isMipmapped, isRepeated, isFiltered }) builds an RGBA texture. UV (0, 0) is the top left of the image. (same as glTF)

Toon material. (shader chunks inserted into ToonRenderer's body shader, the per-game extension point)
- Only patterns or effects that the engine's standard features (texture, light, tint, blending) cannot do go into chunks. Slots without a chunk get the engine's empty function.
- uniformChunk: goes into the top slot of the fragment shader. Write uniforms, constants, functions, and the ins exported by the vertex chunk.
- surfaceChunk: defines void applySurface(inout ToonSurface surface). Called after the engine computes the vertex color, texture and decals, before tint and light.
  ToonSurface { vec3 baseColor (sRGB), float alpha, vec3 emission (linear), vec3 normal (world, unit), float glow (vertex glow), bool isUnlit,
                vec4 detail (vertex pattern index and pattern color), vec2 uv, vec3 localPosition (model coordinates), vec3 worldPosition, vec3 viewDirection (from the surface toward the camera, unit) }
- lightChunk: defines void applyLight(ToonSurface surface, inout ToonLighting lighting). Called after the engine gathers the sun, ambient, fill, rim, point lights and specular, before combining them.
  ToonLighting { vec3 irradiance (light multiplied by the base color), vec3 specular (light added), float shadow (0 ~ 1) }
- vertexChunk: goes into the top slot of the vertex shaders (all three: body, outline, shadow depth) and defines void applyVertex(inout ToonVertex vertex). Called before transforming to world.
  ToonVertex { vec3 localPosition, vec3 localNormal, vec3 color, vec2 material, vec4 detail, vec2 uv, vec4 tint, mat4 modelMatrix }
  User attributes of the instance layout (ToonInstanceLayout) are read as ins of that name. Since it goes into all three, do not use outs that exist only in the body. (use the fields of vertex instead of the vertex attribute names)
  Normals are transformed with mat3(modelMatrix). If the scale is not uniform, divide localNormal by the square of that scale beforehand.
- The shader has the engine's toLinear(vec3) and RECIPROCAL_PI.
- Textures are passed with the draw's options.textures ({ uniform name: texture }). The engine binds them in order to the units it does not use (from 7) and puts the unit into the sampler2D uniform of that name.
- Uniforms that differ per draw are written in options.onBeforeDraw(program, webGL2RenderingContext). The engine rewrites its own uniforms, so write only the material's.

Toon light set. (holds as one bundle the light values ToonRenderer uses to shade bodies)
- The renderer holds one default set, and the renderer's light settings such as setLight modify that set. A different set can be given per draw with options.lightSet. (when the board and the models have different lighting)
- Sun: the direction (sunDirection) is the way the light travels. It is the direction from the sun to the surface, the opposite of the direction pointing from the surface toward the sun. (the direction from position to target of a three.js DirectionalLight)
  The share a surface receives is max(dot(N, -sunDirection), 0). Shining straight down from above is [0, -1, 0].
- Ambient: mixes the sky color and ground color by the normal's up and down (N.y x 0.5 + 0.5). (hemisphere light)
- Fill light (fill): a second directional light that does not receive shadows. Its direction means the same as the sun's. With the default color 0 it is absent.
- Rim light (rim): an edge light pow(1 - max(dot(N, V), 0), power) that grows stronger as the normal turns away from the view direction. Like light, it is multiplied by the base color. With the default strength 0 it is absent.
- Specular: the sun's Blinn-Phong pow(max(dot(N, H), 0), exponent) x strength. It receives shadows. With the default 0 it is absent.
- Point lights: up to TOON_MAXIMUM_POINT_LIGHTS. { position, color (linear), intensity, range, decay, rangeExponent, wrap }
  Attenuation is window x distance attenuation. The window is (1 - (distance / range)^rangeExponent) clamped to 0 ~ 1 and squared if range is greater than 0, and 1 if it is 0. Distance attenuation is 1 / max(distance^decay, 0.01) if decay is greater than 0, and 1 if it is 0.
  The defaults (decay 2, rangeExponent 4) are the point light form of three.js, Unreal and Godot 4. With decay 0 and rangeExponent 1 it becomes the (1 - distance / range)^2 form (Godot 3's attenuation 1).
  The received share is wrap light (dot(N, L) + wrap) / (1 + wrap). (0 is Lambert, the wrap lighting of GPU Gems 1)
- Bands: setBandCount(n) rounds the share received from the sun into n steps. (0 is smooth, the default so far)
  setBandRamp(thresholds, values, half Lambert) splits the share by the thresholds and uses each step's value. With half Lambert, dot x 0.5 + 0.5 is compared to the thresholds, otherwise max(dot, 0). If there is a ramp, the band count is not used. The same bands also apply to the share received from point lights.
- Light model: if setLightModel({ isEnergyNormalized }) is true, base color x light is divided by π. (the textbook Lambert BRDF, the same convention as three.js physical lights, which give light intensity as illuminance, and glTF lights)
  In that case specular is multiplied by the normalized Blinn-Phong factor (exponent + 8) / 8π. With the default false it is base color x light as before.
- All colors are linear colors. (they may exceed 1 for HDR)
- Modifying it raises the version number (getVersion). The renderer does not re-upload if the set and version number are the same.

- Draws ToonRenderer's createMesh result once more with the same matrices to write IDs. Can be used together with the shell outline (ToonRenderer).

- Depth: tells orthographic and perspective apart by the projection matrix. Perspective unpacks depth with the near and far planes and compares distances (meters).

환경 유니폼 적용. (조명 / 앰비언트 / 피부 / 주름 / 마이크로 /: Applies the environment uniforms. (light / ambient / skin / wrinkle / micro / eye / hair parameters)
활성 컴포넌트 적용. (현재 모드에 맞춰 Text / RichText 의: Applies the active component. (toggles setEnable of Text / RichText according to the current mode)
회전 속도 반환. (초당 바퀴 수): Returns the rotation speed. (turns per second)
회전 속도 설정. (초당 바퀴 수): Sets the rotation speed. (turns per second)
회전 속도 최댓값. (초당 라디안, 주지 않으면 최솟값): Maximum angular velocity. (radians per second, the minimum if omitted)
회전 속도. (라디안/초, 음수면 반대로 돈다): Rotation speed. (radians per second, spins the other way if negative)
회전 최댓값. (라디안, 주지 않으면 최솟값): Maximum rotation. (radians, the minimum if omitted)
회전 쿼터니언. (Quaternion 이나 x, y, z, w 를 가진: Rotation quaternion. (a Quaternion or an object with x, y, z, w, must have length 1)
회전각. (라디안, 양수면 화면에서 시계 방향): Rotation angle. (radians, clockwise on screen if positive)
회전체 빔 그리기. (넘긴 차례대로, 축과 두 옆 쪽은 여기서 셈): Draws solid-of-revolution beams. (In the order passed, the axis and two side directions are computed here)
효과 색. (복사해 둔다, null 이면 무시한다): Effect color. (kept as a copy, ignored if null)
효과 설정. (효과별 기본 파라미터 / 색으로 되돌린다): Sets the effect. (resets to the effect's default parameters / color)
효과 없음. (Sprite 와 같게 그린다): No effect. (drawn the same as Sprite)
효과 이름의 적용 차례. (새 배열): Application order of effect names. (a new array)
효과 적용. (씬 postDraw 끝, 화면의 영역을 떠 와 효과를 걸고: Applies the effects. (at the end of the scene's postDraw, captures the screen region, applies the effects and puts it back in the same place)
Returns whether an effect is on.
효과 테의 색 설정. ([r, g, b] 0 ~ 1, 테를 두른 파티클과: Sets the effect rim color. ([r, g, b] 0 ~ 1, edges of rimmed particles and glow ribbons, default is ToonRenderer's default outline color)
효과 파라미터 설정. (효과마다 뜻이 다르다, ShaderSpriteEf: Sets the effect parameters. (meaning differs per effect, see the ShaderSpriteEffect comments)
효과별 파라미터 이름. (타임라인 속성 \"효과.이름\" 으로 접근): Parameter names per effect. (accessed as the timeline property "effect.name")
효과음 내기. (음소거, 첫 누름 전, 받기 전, 다시 낼 간격 안이면: Plays a sound effect. (does not play if muted, before the first press, before downloading, or within the replay interval)
효과음 버스를 만들어 크기를 한꺼번에 걸기: Make a sound effect bus and set the volume all at once
효과음 재생.\n- 다음 차례의 플레이어에 애셋을 실어 재생한다. 그 플:
Plays a sound effect.
- Loads the asset into the next player in turn and plays it. If that player was playing, stops it and plays the new one.
- The volume is this playback's volume (0 ~ 1) multiplied by the pool volume.
효과음 크기. (0 ~ 1 로 자르고, 숫자가 아니면 0): Sound effect volume. (clamped to 0 ~ 1, 0 if not a number)
효과음 풀.\n- 같은 효과음이 연달아 겹쳐 나도 끊기지 않도록, 여러:
Sound effect pool.
- Plays by rotating (round robin) through several AudioPlayers so the same sound effect
  is not cut off when it overlaps in quick succession. (what several games each implemented as a 6-channel pool)
- Usage:
    const pool = new SoundEffectPool(engine.getAudioManager(), 6);
    pool.play(hitAudioAsset);
    pool.play(hitAudioAsset, 0.5);   // half volume for this playback only.
    pool.setVolume(0.8);             // volume of the whole pool. (also multiplied into those playing)
효과음의 버스. (첫 누름 전에는 null): Sound effect bus. (null before the first press)
훑기 시작할 노드. (null 이나 undefined 면 아무것도 하지: Node to start walking from. (does nothing if null or undefined)
훑는 루트 노드. (정하지 않았으면 null): The root node being traversed. (null if not set)
훑을 노드. (자식들도 차례로 훑는다): Node to walk. (its children are walked in turn)
훑을 루트 노드. (보통 씬의 루트): Root node to traverse. (usually the scene root)
휠 값. (스크롤 칸의 wheel 에 그대로 넘긴다): Wheel amount. (passed as is to the scroll view's wheel)
휠 누적값. (휠 스크롤 배율을 곱해 오프셋에서 뺀다, 없으면 아무것도: Accumulated wheel delta. (multiplied by the wheel scroll scale and subtracted from the offset, does nothing if missing)
휠 누적값에 곱할 배율. (기본 1): Multiplier applied to the accumulated wheel delta. (default 1)
휠 세로 값. (WheelEvent.deltaY 의 합, 아래로 굴리면: Vertical wheel amount. (sum of WheelEvent.deltaY, positive when scrolling down)
휠 입력 처리. (TouchRaycaster → UIScrollView):
Handles wheel input. (TouchRaycaster → UIScrollView)
- delta: accumulated mouse wheel value (same sign as DOM WheelEvent's deltaX/deltaY. down = +y)
휠. (Ctrl 을 눌렀는지만 적는다, 키우기와 밀기는 엔진이 넘긴 휠로: Wheel. (only records whether Ctrl was held, zoom and pan are done by the screen from the wheel passed by the engine)
휠을 굴린 자리. (뷰 좌표): Position where the wheel was rolled. (view coordinates)
True if a scroll view received the wheel.
휠을 받을 스크롤 칸 컴포넌트. (없으면 null): The scroll view component to receive the wheel. (null if none)
흐린 결과 텍스처. (핑 판의 컬러 텍스처): Blurred result texture. (the ping target's color texture)
흔들고 잦아드는 오프셋 읽기: Read an offset that shakes and settles
Adds shake.
- If already shaking, the stronger one wins.
흔들림 발생기. (화면 / 노드 공용)\n- 위상이 다른 두 사인파로 x:
Shake generator. (shared by screen / node)
- Builds x / y offsets from two sine waves with different phases and lets them fade out with exponential decay.
  (what several games each reimplemented inline as sin combinations + decay formulas)
- Add strength with addShake(strength), and after tick(dt) every frame add getOffset() to
  the camera or node position.
흔들림 시계 반환. (tick 마다 timeDelta * 속도씩 흐른다): Returns the wobble clock. (advances by timeDelta * speed every tick)
흔들림 시계가 흐르는 빠르기. (초당 라디안, 기본 2): Speed of the wave clock. (radians per second, default 2)
흔들림 진폭. (미터, 가닥 끝일수록 크고 0 이면 없음, 기본 0): Sway amplitude. (meters, larger toward strand tips, none when 0, default 0)
흘릴 시간. (초, 0 이하이면 아무것도 하지 않는다): Time to advance. (seconds, does nothing if 0 or less)
흰색 색상 반환. (이미지/텍스트 출력용 기본 색상): Returns the white color. (default color for image/text output)
흰색 텍스처 반환. (단색 도형용): Returns the white texture. (for solid-color shapes)
흰색으로 구운 글자에 곱할 색. (null 이면 흰색 그대로): Color to multiply text baked in white by. (null keeps it white)
